### 2026-09-22 - ml1310: native Steam sign-in, owned library and downloads in the optional library

Context: the Windows Steam client still does not reach a usable login on device (ml1260–ml1300). The owner obtained permission to publish code derived from Jfishin's private Madeira fork, which added native Steam authentication, library enumeration and depot downloads. Analysis of that fork showed that games there are launched by replacing their Steam API libraries with a Steamworks emulator, injecting the emulator's client library through a loader, and patching Steam's stub DRM at runtime. That launch path is circumvention and was not ported. The owner's rule against altering protection checks applies. Only the authentication, owned-library, depot-download and appmanifest code was adapted. Steam alone decides ownership: depot keys and manifest request codes are issued only for depots the account owns, and downloaded files are unmodified. Games start directly (for titles that do not need Steam running) or through the real Windows Steam client by App ID.

Front end: with MADEIRA_FRONTEND=1 the Library tab shows Steam (installed, downloading, collapsible Not installed) and Other games (existing + flow from folders in drive_c, unchanged artwork matching). Sign-in is a sheet: account name + password, with Steam Guard code and in-app approval offered together, or a QR code (default on iPad) with a same-device hand-off to the Steam app. The same-device hand-off is untested. The token is stored in the Keychain (this device only, while unlocked; service madeira.steam.tokens); Settings has sign-out and library refresh. Install sheet: size, free space, progress/speed/ETA, pause/resume/cancel. Installed entries gain a Steam section: start directly or via the Windows client, program picker, update when the owned build ID advances, uninstall. The Windows client manager moved to Settings.

Destination is C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common with a normal appmanifest, so a later Windows client recognizes the install. The ml1260 client scan now skips entries marked native, so it never rewrites their executable or install state. Installed entries use new optional fields steamNative/steamClientLaunch/steamClientPath/steamBuildID; old library files decode unchanged.

Defects found in the ported code and fixed (generic):
- Download orchestration: whole-install progress (manifests first). The per-depot-manifest chunk journal resumes after pause, failure or termination; a partial last line from a killed write no longer merges with the next key (found by the new host check). Files already on disk are compared chunk by chunk against the chunk SHA-1, so updates fetch only changed data. Files are sized to manifest length. Writes use pwrite on the download tasks (previously on the main actor). A no-cache URLSession keeps 1 MiB chunks out of URLCache. Chunks retry on up to four content servers. Debug manifest/chunk dumps into Documents are removed.
- Paths: manifest names are validated (no traversal, drive or control characters) and directory spelling folds case-insensitively on the case-sensitive iOS volume; the install folder is one sanitized component.
- Depot selection follows the Windows client/DepotDownloader rules (OS, neutral or 64-bit with 32-bit fallback, common or English, no low-violence, DLC, shared redistributable or manifest-less depots). The original downloaded every language and both architectures.
- Decoders: the zstd error-recovery longjmp used one process-wide target while eight chunks decode concurrently; the wrapper is now serialized (TSan reports a data race in the unlocked control). The zstd frame-size query, which runs outside the wrapper and can exit() the app, is no longer used; capacity comes from the manifest. VZip footer sizes are bounded and must match the manifest. The liblzma shim returned success for truncated streams (LZMA_OK) without an output size; it now returns an error. Adler-32 uses zlib's zero-seeded adler32.
- Auth/session: Steam's x-eresult header is checked (wrong password/code and rate limits fail immediately instead of polling empty sessions). Multi-message inflation uses the declared size (a fixed 10x estimate truncated large PICS batches). A logon-denied error distinguishes expired/revoked tokens (sign out with a message) from transient failures. A Keychain write failure is reported instead of leaving a signed-in state that cannot log on.
- Privacy: packet hex dumps, token prefixes, JWT claims, account names and Steam IDs are removed from logs; protocol detail is behind MADEIRA_STEAM_TRACE=1. The content-directory request no longer carries an access token.

Switches: MADEIRA_STEAM_NATIVE=0 (hide native Steam; ml1260 behavior), MADEIRA_LIBRARY_SECTIONS=0 (single grid), MADEIRA_STEAM_PAUSE_FOR_SESSION=0, MADEIRA_STEAM_APPID_FILE=0 (no steam_appid.txt beside new installs), MADEIRA_STEAM_TRACE=1. ### 2026-09-22 - ml1320: HTTPS-capable content servers, zip chunks and attribution

Evidence (logs 154/155, screenshots): QR sign-in succeeded on the second attempt; the first failed with NSURLError -1005 (connection lost). The library reported 523 owned apps, 519 installable on Windows. Installing app 220 started (4 depots, 2584 files) and failed after ~4 s with reason url--1200 (TLS handshake failure). Every later resume (resume=1) failed within ~3 s with reason decompress, including after an app restart.

-1200, proven mechanism: sampling the public GetServersForSteamPipe directory across cells shows CDN entries on *.cdn.steampipe.steamcontent.com with https_support "unavailable", alongside HTTPS-mandatory SteamCache/akamaized servers. The ml1310 filter accepted hosts by name only, so a chunk could be requested over HTTPS from an HTTP-only server. The device's cell list was not logged, so which server failed is not confirmed. Fix: eligibility by https_support (mandatory/optional), use_as_proxy and allowed_app_ids (MADEIRA_STEAM_CDN_FILTER=0 rollback). A per-install ContentHostHealth rotates chunks across servers and demotes a server after repeated failures, with decay on success (MADEIRA_STEAM_HOST_HEALTH=0). The pool is six servers with five attempts per chunk. [steam-cdn] ml1320 reports offered/usable/skipped counts and the first eight demotions.

decompress, likely mechanism (not proven; the log lacked the chunk format): SteamKit's DepotChunk processing handles VZstd, then VZip, then falls back to single-entry PKZip. The port had no zip path, and the failure repeated deterministically on an old depot. Added chunk_zip.c (zlib; deflate/stored; data descriptors; output bounded by the manifest's cb_original; Adler-32/size checks unchanged; MADEIRA_STEAM_ZIP_CHUNKS=0 rollback). Decode failures now report the format (decode-vzip, decode-vzstd, decode-zip<rc> or the leading bytes), so the next log settles it if another encoding is involved.

Also: Steam trace, [steam-play] and [library-sections] lines now go through LogStore. stderr is not captured before a Wine session, which is why [library-sections]/[steam-bridge] were absent from logs 154/155. The install/resume/retry buttons draw their glyphs explicitly: a Label in a bordered button in a Form row rendered title-only.

Attribution: every file derived from Jfishin's Madeira Steam client carries a header ("adapted" or "substantially rewritten"). README.md has a Credits section, and STEAM_INTEGRATION.md states the origin and what Madeira changed or omitted. The ml1320 commit carries a Co-Authored-By trailer for Jfishin (GitHub noreply address from his own commits).

### 2026-09-22 - ml1330: JIT pool while the debugger is attached; start context for threads created suspended

Evidence, first launch: log 156 downloads a game for 7.5 minutes, then Play 14 minutes after JIT was enabled. The log ends at "Allocating 512MB JIT pool via debugger" and the app terminates. Log 148 has the same shape (1 minute after enabling, after the Steam installer download). Logs 150, 153 and 157 allocated within about 15 s of enabling and succeeded (1.8–3.0 s BRK). The existing ml524 note records that iOS ends StikDebug for CPU use about 52 s after it attaches. The launch guard used CS_DEBUGGED, which stays set after the debugger is gone. SIGTRAP was left unhandled because a debugger was attached at start, and Wine's handlers are only installed during a session, so a pool BRK with nobody attached ended the app. The exact termination record is not in the log. The timing correlation (2 of 2 late allocations died, 3 of 3 early ones succeeded) and the code path are the evidence.

Fix (app): the process-lifetime pool (ml962) is allocated as soon as a debugger is observed: at app start when traced, or when Enable JIT completes. The debugger is then detached. Size is madeira-pool.txt, else the previous session's size (persisted), else 512 MB. A later session wanting a different size keeps the early pool, as session 2 always did. The cost is that the pool (jetsam-counted, [no-footprint] applied=false) is resident while browsing the library. "Attached" is now P_TRACED (jit_debugger_attached). Allocation and detach BRKs are never sent without an attached debugger, and a repeated detach is skipped (log 157 shows a second detach BRK at 16:06:27, survivable only because Wine's handler existed by then). The SIGTRAP fallback is armed before any Wine session, never after (Wine owns SIGTRAP from then on). Readiness means a pool exists or a debugger is attached. If JIT was enabled earlier but the debugger has gone, Play reopens StikDebug, takes the pool on attach and resumes the launch in the foreground. Enable JIT waits up to 60 s for a real attach. The library JIT indicator uses the same readiness. Switches: MADEIRA_JIT_EARLY_POOL=0, MADEIRA_JIT_TRACE_GUARD=0, MADEIRA_JIT_RECONNECT=0. Tag: [jit-early] ml1330.

Evidence, stall before the main menu (log 157): about 3.5 FPS during startup/intro with about 248 ms of presenting-thread CPU per frame and about 1 ms GPU (startup JIT warm-up: about 380k blocks compiled in the first windows). The first 10 s window spends 37.7% of CPU in fstatat from find_file_in_dir (case-insensitive lookup on the case-sensitive iOS volume); this recedes in later windows. Then presents stop and CPU drops to 0.15 cores with every guest thread in server waits. Just before that, the main thread (0024) creates three threads with the same start address in the engine's core runtime and parameter, each CREATE_SUSPENDED. It suspends each again (count 1→2) while it is still in startup ([srv-own] init_thread follows the SUSPEND). It then reads 007c's context: "[srv-getctx] #1 tid=007c state=unknown saved_amd64 flags=0 rip=0x0 rsp=0x0". A cross-thread SetThreadContext follows (the first of the session), and none of the three threads is ever resumed. Thread 007c stays parked in wait_suspend.

Root cause (code, wine/server/thread.c): suspend_thread skips stop_thread for an already-suspended thread, so the first read goes through get_thread_context → stop_thread. On iOS that took an immediate Mach snapshot (ios_snapshot) of a thread that had not yet posted its start context, producing zeros. When the thread then reached wait_suspend and posted its real context, select refused it (a context existed and was not STATUS_PENDING → invalid_param), losing the correct start context. The set side also skips its in-thread application path for snapshot contexts. Upstream leaves the context pending until the target posts it.

Fix (wine 6ecc4c3d0b8): threads created suspended are marked ios_start_pending. The mark is cleared when they post their context through select, or at init_thread if they are told not to park. It is initialised explicitly because mem_alloc poisons new objects. While marked, stop_thread leaves the context pending (not a snapshot): the reader waits on the context sync and receives the self-posted context. init_thread already tells a thread with a pending context to park, so it always posts. A SetThreadContext made meanwhile is cached and applied by the thread on resume (the existing upstream path). MADEIRA_CTX_START_WAIT=0 restores the immediate snapshot. [ctx-start] ml1330 reports the switch, the first eight deferred reads and the first eight completed posts. This is a proven mechanism for the garbage context and the lost post. That it is what stopped this program's startup is strongly indicated but device-unverified. The startup frame rate is JIT warm-up plus file lookups and is not claimed improved.

Validation: native Wine rebuilt (ntdll 35/35, win32u 46/46, server). Workspace sources match, and libwineserver.a contains the three [ctx-start] ml1330 strings and ios_ctx_start_wait_enabled. The existing Steam host checks still pass. The IPA printed "IPA verified". .xtool/verify-ml1330.py passes 79 checks: generated-source and native-stub sync (ContentView, StikJITHelper, JITAllocator), new tags and switches in the Mach-O, archive freshness, and 1365 entries identical to ml1320 except the executable. No host model of the server handshake was built. No Wine, game or iOS session ran on this PC.

Device test: cold-start Madeira from StikDebug. The log should show "[jit-early] ml1330 trigger=start ... pool=ready ... detached=1" within seconds. Browse or download for several minutes, then press Play: no allocation should occur ("reuse ... no debugger round trip"). Separately, start the same game again and wait at its intro. Expect "[ctx-start] ml1330 ... read before its start" and "... posted its start context", and the menu should appear. If it stalls, send the log with [ctx-start], [srv-suspend], [srv-getctx], [srv-setctx] and [thread-stacks].

### 2026-09-22 - ml1350: Windows client transport socket events; handled-fault storm terminal

Device evidence (Windows client, log 162 plus the client's own cef_log.txt, webhelper.txt, connection_log.txt and bootstrap_log.txt; HL2 set to start through the client, which ran with -applaunch 220): the client is current (build 1769731672), its connectivity test passes, and the browser helper starts, creates its shared JS context and loads the UI frame. It then shows "Unexpected Transport Error (0x3000)". In every client run since installation (six runs in cef_log.txt), each connection attempt to ws://localhost:6246x/transportsocket/ logs two "Unknown error 10038 mapped to net::ERR_FAILED" lines. 10038 is WSAENOTSOCK. The server shows the same attempts reaching the kernel correctly: [srv-conn] owner=96 to ::1 is refused (err=61), then 127.0.0.1 completes with peer=YES, and steam.exe's listener reports [acc-ready] for each one. So the connection exists, and the failure happens after it.

Root cause (source chain, not device-observed directly): after a connect completes, Chromium calls WSAEnumNetworkEvents(socket, event, ...). Wine's ws2_32 implements that as IOCTL_AFD_GET_EVENTS, passing the event HANDLE as the InputBuffer argument with an input size of 0, following the Windows AFD convention. The iOS WoW64 thunk converts every buffer argument with guest_ptr32, so the 32-bit helper's handle arrives as B + handle, where B is the window base. wine_server_obj_handle() maps any value that does not fit in 32 bits to 0xfffffff0, the server's get_event_obj fails, the ioctl returns STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE and ws2_32 maps that to WSAENOTSOCK. Both addresses fail the same way, which matches two errors per URL. Only 32-bit callers that pass an event are affected. The client's own networking (TLS, CDN) does not use this path, which is why its connectivity test passes.

Fix: the unix-side IOCTL_AFD_GET_EVENTS handler undoes the window offset for that argument alone, and only for a 32-bit caller (ios_wow_base() nonzero) when the value lies inside that caller's window. NULL, native callers and out-of-window values are unchanged. This is in native ntdll, where getenv works; the PE-side WoW64 thunk cannot read Madeira switches. MADEIRA_AFD_EVENT_HANDLE=0 keeps the converted value. [afd-event-handle] ml1350 logs the first eight conversions. The host check composes the production guest_ptr32, afd_event_handle_arg and wine_server_obj_handle. Rollback reproduces 0xfffffff0; with the fix, handles round-trip in four windows.

Separate device evidence (log 161, a 64-bit Unity game): the app terminated through "[redeliv] 2000 identical redeliveries ... terminating the TASK". The faults are managed-runtime null checks (read of address 0 in freshly allocated JIT code) that the runtime handles and resumes from. Every 64-frame interval from line 15194 to the end contains 551-644 deliveries across the same 8 sites on one thread, while presents continue at a 26-40 ms average gap. The ml461 terminal counted identical (thread,pc,addr) deliveries cumulatively, so a site hit once per frame reached 2000 in roughly a minute and killed the task. Fix: a run of identical deliveries continues only when the same thread's previous delivery had the same key and arrived within 8 ms. A fault elsewhere, or a pause, is progress and restarts the count. A real storm resumes and refaults at once, so it still reaches the terminal. MADEIRA_REDELIV_PROGRESS=0 restores cumulative counting. [redeliv-progress] ml1350 logs the first eight resets of runs of 64 or more. No timing record exists for the ml452-ml465 storms, so the 8 ms bound is a design choice, not a measured storm rate. A storm slower than 8 ms per iteration would no longer be terminated by this path. The host check covers a fast storm, a storm at the bound, two threads storming, the log-161 pattern, one site per frame at 144 FPS, a pause, and rollback.

Also examined in log 161, with no change: the game's custom cursor disappears because the game hides it (ShowCursor off, [cursor-visibility] guest-show=0) and clips the cursor to the centre point ({640,360,640,360}), after which relative mouse mode takes over. That is the program's own request. Whether it is intended or a consequence of its script exceptions cannot be told from the log.

Not claimed: that the Windows client now reaches its login screen. The transport error has a demonstrated cause and fix, but the earlier open problems in STEAM_CEF_HANDOFF.md (tile-displaced rendering, the libcef crash site, CM login above TCP) may appear next. HL2 through the client, login and -applaunch remain device-unverified. Nothing bypasses Steam's requirements.

### 2026-09-22 - ml1360: 32-bit winproc handles, accept-trace budgets and silent client launches

Device results for ml1350 (logs prev 15 and 163; cef_log (2).txt; screenshot): the transport fix is confirmed. No "Unknown error 10038" appears in any of the four new client runs, [afd-event-handle] ml1350 shows handles such as raw=0x7200000a64 -> 0xa64, and both ws://localhost transport URLs connect. In the first session the login window appeared, as the owner reported, and then froze. In the second no login window appeared. The console line "WSALookupServiceBegin failed with: 8" is Chromium's network-change notifier falling back (ml1300 analysis) and is not the failure.

Freeze (log prev 15): the helper's UI thread (tid 0064, teb 0x7200300000) faults with FEX "NoExec instruction in entry block: FFFF0036", reached through NtUserSetWindowPos -> send_message -> call_window_proc -> KeUserModeCallback. It is followed by 6770 "dispatch_user_callback ignoring exception c0000005", later also at 0xffff0038. Every message to the window failed inside its callback and was dropped, so the window could not paint or take input. Eventually the ml461 terminal ended the helper (2000 identical deliveries within the 8 ms run rule) and the client restarted it. 0xffff0036 is a Wine winproc handle (WINPROC_HANDLE << 16 | index), above the 18 built-in procedures. Source chain: wow64win converts win_proc_params.func for NtUserMessageCall(NtUserCallWindowProc) and WNDCLASSEX.lpfnWndProc for NtUserRegisterClassExWOW with guest_ptr32. win32u's get_winproc_ptr accepts only values whose bits above 16 equal 0xffff, so B + 0xffff0036 was treated as a plain procedure. get_winproc_params then returned it as procA/procW, host_ptr32 truncated it back to 0xffff0036, and user32 called it as code. A 32-bit CallWindowProc with a handle (as returned by Get/SetWindowLongPtr for procedures used across character sets) therefore always failed. Fix: win32u (build/win32u-unix/class_ios.c) recognizes, for a 32-bit caller, a value inside that caller's window whose offset has the handle form. The top 64 KB of a 32-bit address space never holds code. Other values, other windows and native callers are unchanged. This is done in native win32u because the PE-side thunks cannot read Madeira switches. MADEIRA_WINPROC_HANDLE=0 disables it; [winproc-handle] ml1360 logs the first eight conversions. Host check: the production helper and get_winproc_ptr, composed with the wow64win guest_ptr32, resolve offset handles in four windows. The 16-bit range is preserved, real procedures and out-of-window values are not treated as handles, and rollback reproduces the unrecognized handle.

Second session (log 163): no fault storm. Both transports were established (tcp-enum ESTAB, peers on 63176/63178). Chromium reconnected to 63171 about 11 s later and from then on attempted only ::1 (refused, err=61), never 127.0.0.1, until the client's transport error. Its first connection to that port had used 127.0.0.1 after the ::1 refusal. The drop's cause is not established. One plausible mechanism, not verified: Chromium's WebSocket endpoint lock holding the IPv4 endpoint while the old socket is not fully released. The ml1300 accept trace could not help because 24 "queued" lines used its whole budget. Queued now has 6 lines and outcomes 48, and the AcceptEx first-data stage is recorded (recv-wait; delivered with a byte count; recv-failed with status). Metadata only, same switch MADEIRA_SOCKET_ACCEPT_TRACE=0, tag [socket-accept] ml1360.

Front-end: a game launch through the Windows client adds -silent before -applaunch, so Steam's library window stays closed while sign-in, Steam Guard and error windows still appear. Open Steam and steam://install launches are unchanged. MADEIRA_STEAM_SILENT=0 restores the window; [steam-silent] ml1360 records the setting. Host Steam launch checks cover default, rollback and install route. The requested fully hidden flow (sign-in and game start behind the loading screen) is not implemented. The Windows client keeps its own sign-in, which must be completed once in its window. Madeira does not write its native token into the client's encrypted credential store. The console window titled steamwebhelper.exe is created by the helper itself (conhost --server, spawned from tid 0064), most likely because of Madeira's injected diagnostic --enable-logging flag. It stays because Chromium release builds only write cef_log.txt with that flag.

Transport Error: 2", so the connection-manager path works only intermittently. This is STEAM_CEF_HANDOFF §2.3. Its cause is not established this round; the evidence feed below is aimed at it. The second steam.exe in log 165 had no arguments: it came from the desktop icon, handed off to the running client and exited.

Refuted: Wine's crypt32 does have root certificates on iOS ([crypt32-ios] imported 121 from the bundled cacert.pem). The "Steam no longer supports running on 32-bit Windows" banner and the 32-bit browser (cef.win7) match Steam's behavior on real Windows-on-ARM64 PCs. The banner is not treated as a defect, and no x64 identity is faked. Noted but not changed: ProcessWow64Information for the current process returns the session-global wow_peb, which later holds a sibling's PEB32 (same guest offset, so the value is still non-zero and matches). It could read 0 after a sibling's window is released.

LSE atomics (log 165): the browser UI thread took a write fault on LDADDAL w5, w5, [x24] (0xb8e50305, x86 LOCK XADD) to 0x7225f21004 in a page mapped RX because it also holds translated code, inside destroy_window -> call_window_proc. "[store-undecoded] ... ADD THIS ENCODING" followed, and the fault reached the guest twice as an access violation. The ml626 SWP emulator had deliberately deferred the rest of the family until it appeared. ios_lse_atomic_op now performs LD<op>/ST<op> (ADD, CLR, EOR, SET, SMAX, SMIN, UMAX, UMIN; all sizes) with real atomics on the RW alias of the same physical page. Rt receives the zero-extended old value, and Rt=31 is the store alias. Unaligned addresses are refused, and SWP (o3=1), CAS and plain stores are not claimed. MADEIRA_ALIAS_LSE_ATOMICS=0 restores the previous behavior; [lse-emul] ml1370 logs the first eight. Host check: every opcode and size, the device instruction's exact result, operand masking, neighbouring bytes untouched, refusals, and 8 threads x 100000 concurrent adds with no lost update.

Evidence feeds (no behavior change for guests):
- Steam connection log. The error mirror's single 32-line budget went to Chromium VERBOSE mDNS lines, and connection_log.txt was never eligible. Lines written to connection_log.txt that mention connect/logged/timeout/cm or an error word are now mirrored as [steam-connlog] ml1370, up to 96 on their own budget. [U:1:n] SteamIDs become [U:1:#] and dotted IPv4 addresses become x.x.x.x; ports, host names and other numbers are kept. Chromium ":VERBOSE" lines no longer use the error budget. MADEIRA_STEAM_LOG_MIRROR=0 restores the ml1300 mirror. The host check covers redaction of real line shapes and non-address numbers.
- Loopback transport. The ml1360 accept trace shows every local transport connection completing on the listener side (completing, accepted, delivered with 0 first-data bytes, because AcceptEx requests no data). That includes log 166, where the browser gave up on both after 11 s without a window and then retried only ::1. [loopback-io] ml1370 records the first six send/receive byte counts and hard errors per loopback connection: direction, byte count and ports only, 120 lines total, and at most 100000 checks so ordinary traffic stops paying the two socket queries. MADEIRA_LOOPBACK_IO_TRACE=0 disables. The host check runs on real loopback TCP sockets.

### 2026-09-22 - ml1380: Steam connection-manager failure narrowed; crypt32 verdict diagnostic; JIT pool exhaustion in the client UI

Device result for ml1370 (log 167 and a screenshot). HL2 launched through the Windows client now reaches Steam's pre-launch step, "Unable to Sync" (cloud saves), with the status bar at NO CONNECTION. The dialog's "Play anyway" did not respond. [lse-emul] ml1370 handled the browser UI thread's LDADDAL twice, and no [store-undecoded] appeared, so ml1370's fix is confirmed. [loopback-io] and [socket-accept] show the transport healthy in this run.

Steam connection manager ([steam-connlog] ml1370, 96 lines, masked): the GetCMListForConnect Web API call fails with "status = 0" after 8, 43 and 32 s. Each round then pings cmp1-iad1 (27018, 443) and cmp1-lax1 (27018); all fail in the same second with "timeout/neterror - Invalid", and Connect() reports ConnectFailed('Connection Failed':0) with port 0. The HTTP connectivity test to test.steampowered.com passes every time. Madeira side: [srv-conn] shows the TCP connects completing to real peers, and [sock-tl] shows the TLS 1.3 handshake completing (597 bytes sent including the client Finished, ~4.5 KB received, no alert), after which the client sends nothing and closes. This is ml590's "no WebSocket Upgrade" observation, now in context. The TLS library accepted the peer, and the application then rejected it. At that moment cryptnet runs in steam.exe (CryptnetUrlCache writes, a blocking port-80 fetch), which shows CryptoAPI chain building with URL retrieval. A Steam Community thread from the 2021 root expiry shows Steam depending on the Windows root store. Conclusion (inference, not observed directly): steam.exe rejects the connection-manager and Web API certificates through crypt32.

Steam's servers now present Let's Encrypt's 2026 "Gen Y" chains, checked with openssl from the development PC. cmp1-iad1.steamserver.net: leaf <- YE2 <- Root YE (cross-signed by ISRG Root X2, from May 13 2026) <- X2 (cross-signed by X1). api.steampowered.com: leaf <- YR1 <- Root YR (cross-signed by ISRG Root X1). OpenSSL validates both using only Madeira's cacert.pem (Mozilla, May 2026; contains X1 and X2, not the self-signed Root YE/YR). YE2's issuer URL http://ye.i.lencr.org/ serves the cross-signed Root YE (the same SHA-256 fingerprint 0FC0901C...). So a chain built by URL retrieval also reaches X2, and "missing Gen-Y roots" is refuted. No certificate was added. Remaining candidates: revocation (CRL distribution points ye2.c.lencr.org/117.crl, ye.c.lencr.org, x2.c.lencr.org; no OCSP), ECDSA P-384 signature verification through bcrypt, or SSL policy. The same failure predates the Gen-Y switch (STEAM_CEF_HANDOFF §2.3, ml559 era), which argues against an issue specific to the new chain.

Diagnostic: crypt32's CertGetCertificateChain logs the first 16 chains per process ([cert-chain] ml1380: error/info status, flags including revocation requests, whether an additional store was supplied, chain and element counts). Chains with errors also list up to six elements per chain with their simple display names and status. CertVerifyCertificateChainPolicy logs the first 16 failures ([cert-policy] ml1380: policy, error, failing chain and element, flags, SSL server name and checks). Names and status bits only. This is PE code, which cannot read Madeira switches, so it uses Wine's err channel: WINEDEBUG=err-chain turns it off. Built for i386 (the client is 32-bit), aarch64 and arm64ec, and verified in all three packaged DLLs.

UI freeze: at t+90 s the browser's UI thread (tid 00f0) needed a new FEX code buffer. The 896 MB pool's tail held 32 carves (738 MB) with none free, against a budget of 739 MB (pool minus 61 MB head minus 96 MB margin). Refusals halved the request down to 1 MB, and the thread took the designed honest fault at 0xdead ("EXEC ALLOC FAILED ... forcing honest fault"). That thread ends, which is why "Play anyway" stopped responding. Earlier client sessions (logs 162–166, up to 240 s) never refused, so the demand depends on the UI's workload; here the Store page was open behind the dialog. With around 110 threads, some thread is always parked in an older code-buffer generation, so no carve is released (free=0 throughout). The pool cannot simply grow: 896 MB is the jetsam-proven ceiling in ContentView, and this session already peaked at 3.26 GB physical footprint with 1.5 GB compressed. No pool policy is changed on one data point. HL2 itself would also need pool space in the same session. This is a real limit of running the full Windows client plus its Chromium UI plus a game in one process.

### 2026-09-22 - ml1400: shared crypt32 host-root enumeration wiped the Windows root store (Steam client NO CONNECTION)

Device result for ml1390 (log 169, screenshot): same "Please update these games first: 220". The new diagnostics answered both open questions.

Root cause of NO CONNECTION (STEAM_CEF_HANDOFF §2.3): [cert-chain] ml1380 in steam.exe (pid 0034) shows early chains (threads 0044, 00f0; 4 elements, additional store given) with error 0. Every later api.steampowered.com chain (thread 0124, flags 0x48000001 = end-cert cache plus chain revocation excluding the root) builds correctly (leaf <- YR1 <- Root YR <- ISRG Root X1, no revocation bits) but ends with CERT_TRUST_IS_UNTRUSTED_ROOT (0x20) on ISRG Root X1 (info 0x0c: self-signed, name match). No [cert-policy] failure is logged, so the client rejects on the chain status itself. Source chain: build/crypto-unix/crypt32_unixlib_ios.c enum_root_certs, like upstream, hands out the head of the host-root list and frees it. That is correct when every process has its own unix side. In Madeira all pseudo-processes share one, so the first process to import roots (steam.exe: [crypt32-ios] loaded 121 once) consumed the list. The next process to import (the browser helper, whose crypt32 attached at line 4206) got STATUS_NO_MORE_ENTRIES at once. rootstore.c sync_trusted_roots_from_known_locations then treated every root it had imported earlier but no longer saw on the host as removed there, and deleted them from HKLM\Software\Microsoft\SystemCertificates\Root. The crypt32_root_semaphore only serializes concurrent imports; each process still imports once. Later chains in steam.exe therefore lacked X1 and X2, and the Web API call, the CM pings and the auth session all failed after completed TLS handshakes. This explains the whole ml590–ml1390 symptom set, including why a first login sometimes got through (before the second process's import). It is inferred from source plus the verdicts, not from a registry dump.

Fix: the host list is loaded once under a lock and kept for the session. Each enumerating thread gets its own position, which advances only when a certificate was copied (the PE loop asks again with a larger buffer). The position is dropped at STATUS_NO_MORE_ENTRIES and restarts after 10 s idle, so an interrupted enumeration cannot truncate a later one. The PE side and the parameter struct are unchanged. MADEIRA_ROOT_ENUM_SHARED=0 restores consuming enumeration. [root-enum] ml1400 logs the first 16 completed enumerations with the count served. Host check (production source, fake bundle of 121 certificates with sizes above the 2048-byte first buffer, real threads, fake clock): two processes and repeated imports each receive all 121 in order; the buffer-growth retry works; an idle restart works; a quick continuation resumes; the bundle loads once. Rollback reproduces the device failure (second caller gets 0). The user's registry already lost the imported roots; the next session's first import re-adds them all as new.

Update refusal: [steam-contentlog] ml1390 "Failed running app 220 (required app 380 not ready)". [steam-acf] ml1390 shows the client rewrote Madeira's record: StateFlags 6 (update required + fully installed), TargetBuildID 0, InstalledDepots 221/222/233/234 as Madeira wrote them, and SharedDepots 340>340, 380>380, 389>380, 420>420 added by the client. The current HL2 (hl2_complete) depends on Lost Coast, Episode One and Episode Two content that Steam installs as apps 340, 380 and 420 in the same folder. Madeira's installer skipped those depots (no manifest of their own in app 220's PICS; "depotfromapp"). Once the client connects it can download them itself. A native-installer follow-up (install depotfromapp content and write the owning apps' install records) is not done this round. SteamAppInfo now parses depotfromapp and the selection log marks such depots (<appid); install behavior is unchanged.

Validation: 10 host suites pass (ASan/UBSan), native ntdll 35/35 and win32u 46/46, and the IPA printed "IPA verified". .xtool/verify-ml1400.py passes 23 checks: sync, archive and binary tags, cacert.pem unchanged, and only the executable changed. Build catch: the first build of this round reported success but did not contain the fix. .xtool/build-wine-native.sh synced build/ntdll-unix, win32u-unix and wineserver into the workspace but not build/crypto-unix, so the exported HEAD copy of crypt32_unixlib_ios.c was compiled. The content check caught it (archive and binary lacked [root-enum]). crypto-unix is now in the local sync list; its last committed change (Sep 11) predates the workspace export, so no earlier round shipped stale code from it. No Wine, Steam or Windows program ran on this PC. The CM connection, login persistence and the episode dependency download are device-unverified.

### 2026-09-23 - ml1410: wineserver use-after-free on cancelling a dead thread's I/O (whole-session freeze); loopback wait trace; license-aware depot keys

Device result for ml1400 (logs 170-172, screenshots). Proven: the root-store fix works. In log 170 steam.exe fetched GetCMListForConnect (10 Netfilter + 99 WebSocket CMs), pinged the WebSocket CMs (~320-360 ms) and logged on ("RecvMsgClientLogOnResponse() : processing complete"), then started the 340/380/420 content downloads. The CM connection dropped once ("ConnectionDisconnected('I/O Operation Failed')", 27018 WebSocket) with no socket error logged around it, and the client logged on again by itself 9 s later. Not addressed this round.

Freeze (log 170): the user saw a Cloud Error toast, then no input worked. The wineserver thread faulted at req_cancel_async+0x158 (ldp x9,x8,[x20]; str x8,[x9,#8] = list_remove of async->process_entry right after cancel_async() in cancel_process_async), right after "[srv-own] read_request EOF tid=0240 pid=0060 -> kill_thread" (a browser-process thread exiting). kill_thread, unlike the terminate_thread request, does not cancel the thread's asyncs. Inferred path (from source, not logged): cancel_async -> async_terminate -> thread_queue_apc does not queue the completion (owner TERMINATED; the other-thread fallback needs a thread in APC wait or one that accepts a signal) -> APC destroy -> async_set_result -> the queue drops its reference -> the last reference goes inside cancel_async, and the list_remove writes through freed memory. Fix (wine/server/async.c): cancel_process_async holds a reference on each async across cancel_async and releases it after putting the async back on the process list. An async whose final result was stored during its own cancellation gets no async_cancel attached. Otherwise the cancel wait would never be signaled, and async_destroy asserts that none is attached. Completion is tracked with an explicit ios_completed bit set in async_set_result. The signaled bit cannot be used, because async_wake_obj already signals a pending non-blocking async. MADEIRA_ASYNC_CANCEL_HOLD=0 restores the old loop. [async-cancel] ml1410 logs the first 8 synchronous completions with the owner thread and whether it is gone. Host check: the production cancel_process_async runs under ASan against a model of async_terminate/async_set_result/async_destroy. It covers the device case (gone owner, cancel from another thread), a pending already-signaled async, a cancel from the owning thread whose APC cannot be queued (no wait object, cancel released), the normal pending case (wait handle, signaled on completion) and an untouched async on another file. The rollback reproduces heap-use-after-free in cancel_process_async.

Transport error (log 171, the relaunch): "Unexpected Transport Error ... during startup (0x3000)" with restart options. LogOn() was never called. That dialog belongs to the loopback transport between steam.exe (pid 0034, listener) and steamwebhelper (pid 0060). Both AcceptEx listeners (52649, 52650) accepted and delivered. The helper sent its 554-byte upgrade request on both (fd 1285 -> 52650, fd 487 -> 52649). steam.exe read and answered 52650 (554/129/314/21) and never logged a read on 52649. In logs 169/170 both connections were read immediately, and the lower port carries the 27 KB exchange. The same single steam.exe thread creation precedes the reads in all three logs. Later helper retries to 52649 show only refused [::1] connects ([srv-conn] has a budget, so absent IPv4 retries are not evidence). [afd-event-handle] lines carry the 0x72 window base (browser process) and are capped at 8, so they say nothing about steam.exe. Stale-fd theory set aside: upstream keeps unconnected stream sockets out of the fd cache until accept_into_socket. Open: steam.exe never requested the data, requested it and was never woken, or was woken without data. New evidence: [loopback-wait] ml1410 in the wineserver, for stream sockets with a loopback peer only. It logs the recv_socket verdict (status, nonblocking, force_async, queue state), each AFD poll request (mask, events, immediate revents, flags, wait), poll completion and the read-queue wake. The cap is 12 lines per socket and 160 total, and the pid is 0 in main-loop context (MADEIRA_LOOPBACK_WAIT_TRACE=0). ntdll adds [loopback-io] ml1410 recv-would-block: the first receive per loopback connection that would block, never on sends (still under MADEIRA_LOOPBACK_IO_TRACE).

Depot keys (log 172): installing another owned game from Madeira's library failed three times with "[steam-depot] ml1310 failed app=... reason=depot-key", 140 ms after the CDN list (the first key request). Valve's DepotDownloader leaves out depots the account's licenses do not include. Madeira now reads the licensed depot IDs ("depotids" in the package info the library already fetches, cached per session). It skips a refused depot only if the licenses do not include it, and still fails on any other refusal or when nothing is left (MADEIRA_STEAM_LICENSE_DEPOTS=0 fails on every refusal). [steam-depot] ml1410 depot-key refused logs app, depot and EResult. [steam-depot] ml1410 license logs skipped and kept depots. The ml1390 selection line now comes before the key requests, so a refusal still shows the layout. The empty-plan case keeps its original depotNotFound error. Device-unverified. If the refused depot is licensed, the cause is elsewhere, and the new line will name it.

Native ntdll 35/35, win32u 46/46, wineserver async + sock compiled, and the IPA printed "IPA verified". .xtool/verify-ml1410.py passes 36 checks: workspace sync, archive and binary tags, generated Swift in sync, cacert.pem unchanged, same entry list as ml1400, only the executable changed. Device results (logs 173-176, prev16, screenshots). Logs 173 and prev16 were still the ml1400 build: no ml1410 tag appears, and every client launch writes `[loopback-wait]`. Log 173 (client) logged on in 1 s and started downloading apps 340/380/420 plus 220's own update (~3.8 GB total). The earlier "667 MB" was only 220's share. The CM connection stayed healthy.

Client logon stall (log 175, ml1410 build). Proven:
- The loopback transport completed. Both connections and the 27 KB exchange show in the new `[loopback-wait]` lines: steam.exe does non-blocking forced-async receives, woken by `wake-read`.
- No LogOn() happened in 5 minutes.
- The early JIT pool was 512 MB. It is sized at app start from the previous session's request, which was a direct launch, and the client session asks for 896 MB. Result: `TAIL REFUSED` for FEX EC_CODE, then `EXEC ALLOC FAILED ... honest fault at 0xdead` (line 12387).
- From line ~13146 on, Chrome_IOThread in the browser process sat at ~70% of a core, jit 0%, in 35 of 37 profiler windows.
  - Thread stacks: aarch64 ntdll RVAs 0x67c20 / 0x777c4 / 0x3fc48 (virtual_unwind, RtlLookupFunctionEntry, LdrFindEntryForAddress), constant sp=0x174ffdbf0.
  - ios_jit_reverse_translate_addr was the top profile entry at 41-46% of all CPU. Its loop index was small, so lookups succeeded and it was simply called endlessly.
  - The sessions that logged on (170, 173) show no such thread.

Inferred: the 0xdead fault frame lies outside every image and cannot be unwound. call_seh_handlers and RtlUnwindEx stop only at a NULL or invalid frame or the stack base, so a step that changes neither Pc nor Sp repeats forever.

Fixes:
- (1) The early pool is remembered as the largest recent session's size, and a library with Windows Steam client entries starts at 896 MB or more. MADEIRA_POOL_STICKY_MAX=0; `[jit-early] ml1420`.
- (2) signal_arm64.c ios_unwind_stalled: three identical Pc/Sp steps end the walk. The handler search then returns STATUS_UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION, and RtlUnwindEx raises STATUS_INVALID_DISPOSITION. The switch MADEIRA_UNWIND_GUARD=0 is read only once a stall is seen. `[unwind-stall] ml1420` logs pc/lr/sp/fp, up to 16 lines.
- (3) ios_jit_reverse_translate_addr rejects addresses outside the pool at once, tries the last hit first, and never matches freed slots (pe_base NULL; the old scan did). The switch is read at image registration, because the lookup runs on the PE caller's stack through a tail branch. MADEIRA_JIT_REV_FAST=0; `[jit-rev] ml1420`.

Host checks:
- check-unwind-stall: stops after three no-progress steps, never stops a progressing walk, caps its log, rollback keeps walking.

  - FEX's Mono backpatcher would self-deadlock on CodeInvalidationMutex if it wrote a trapped page without an alias.

- An x64/x86 device test: RWX store throughput, patch-without-flush, and PAGE_EXECUTE_READ write raising an AV.

### 2026-09-23 - ml1430: WoW64 syscall parking for the code-buffer sweeper (Windows Steam client pool exhaustion)

Device result for ml1420 (log 177, screenshot). Device-verified:
- The Library found the previously missing owned app (lowercase PICS type).
- After "Show live log" the starting screen now dismisses, and its buttons respond.
- The starting screen showed the client's download progress (202 MB of 3.8 GB, 5%, 4 apps pending).
- The early pool was 896 MB ("last session"), and the new unwind guard fired once (`[unwind-stall] ml1420 dispatch code=c0000005 pc=lr=1373f8160`) instead of spinning.

Then the desktop froze within about a minute. Proven from the log:
- The pool tail was 720 MB: 30 live carves (17 × 32 MB, 11 × 16 MB, 2 × 16 KB) with 0 free, against a budget of 713 MB and a head of 85 MB.
- `TAIL REFUSED` ×4, then `EXEC ALLOC FAILED ... honest fault at 0xdead` on tid 02b4 (third pseudo-process, window 0x73).
- That delivery `HOLDS FEX shared lock` (`[deliver-hold]`), so every thread of that process that needed code waited forever.
- The per-process code buffers rotated repeatedly: `[code-buffer] recycled #N ... pinned=15..30`, one process at gen 16.
- There were no `[gen-sweep]` lines at all.

Root cause, proven from source:
- CodeBufferManager is per process, and a generation lives while any thread's CurrentCodeBuffer holds it.
- The ml460 sweeper (CPUBackend.cpp IosMaybeSweepCodeBuffers) migrates only registered threads that are outside emitted code. Only the ARM64EC frontend registers threads (Module.cpp:1998, InSimulation, cleared on syscall exits).
- In the WoW64 frontend a syscall is `blr` out of the emitted block (BranchOps.cpp DEF_OP(Syscall)): the handler runs Wow64SystemServiceEx with a return address into its generation on the stack. Every blocked WoW64 thread therefore pinned a generation for as long as it waited.
- steam.exe and every steamwebhelper are 32-bit, and Chromium parks hundreds of threads.

Fix (FEX WOW64 Module.cpp, FEXCore CPUBackend.cpp; `xtajit.dll` rebuilt):
- FEXCore: IosSweepRegisterThreadEx adds an optional per-thread Migrated flag, which the sweep sets under the gate when IosRemoteMigrateStale returns 1. IosSweepRegisterThread delegates with nullptr, so the ARM64EC module is unchanged and not rebuilt.
- BTCpuThreadInit registers the thread (IosInSim=1, Migrated) and points Pointers.SyscallHandlerFunc at IosWowSyscallEntry, a naked stub that passes the caller SP.
- IosWowSyscallC arms parking only in these cases:
  - for the outermost syscall (depth 0; restored from a local, so a long-jumped nested call cannot leave it raised);
  - when Frame->ReturningStackLocation lies 0..8 KB above the caller SP and is 16-aligned (a stale deeper value left by a long-jumped callback is declined);
  - when DispatcherLoopTopFillSRA is known.
- HandleSyscallImpl parks around WineUnixCall and Wow64SystemServiceEx after UnlockJITContext: `IosInSim=0` with a release store. It unparks before LockJITContext: `IosInSim=1`, seq_cst fence, spin while IosCodeBufferSweepGate (the Dekker pair of the ARM64EC funnels). BTCpuSimulateImpl unparks too, so a callback that re-enters simulation is never movable.
- When moved, the C side restores ReturningStackLocation and clears InSyscallInfo. The stub switches SP to the dispatcher's, zeroes x1 (ENTRY_FILL_SRA_SINGLE_INST_REG on non-EC) and branches to LoopTopFillSRA.
- Why this is equivalent to returning (all verified in source and asserted by the host test):
  - The bridges are `int 0x2e` (0x2ecd2ecd), INT carries DEFAULT_SYSCALL_FLAGS, and FLAGS_BLOCK_END holds on _WIN32. INTOp routes 0x2E to SyscallOp on WoW64.
  - SyscallOp ends with `ExitFunction(LoadContext(rip))`, and OS_GENERIC writes no result.
  - The emitted tail only restores SP, runs FillStaticRegs (all masks), clears InSyscallInfo and pops dynamic registers, which are dead at the block end.
  - LoopTopFillSRA refills every static register and dispatches at State.rip. Callee-saved registers (STATE x28, PF/AF x26/x27, callret x25) are restored by the C epilogue before the stub branches.
- BTCpuThreadTerm unregisters before freeing the frontend data (IosSweepUnregisterThread waits out a sweep in flight).
- MADEIRA_WOW_SYSCALL_SWEEP=0 restores the old behaviour exactly (no registration, the original handler pointer). `[wow-sweep] ml1430` logs the switch state once per process, the first 8 resumes then every 1024th, and the first 4 declines. `[gen-sweep]` now also counts WoW64 moves.
- The stub was checked by disassembly of the built module: mov x3,sp; stp; bl IosWowSyscallC; ldp; cbnz x0; ret; mov sp,x0; mov x16,x1; mov x1,#0; br x16.

UI:
- The Library screen (where the JIT/Memory+ dots are) now shows the build label.
- The HUD's top overlays (download banner, session message, live log) use the larger of the reported safe-area inset and the status bar height. In portrait the reported inset was 0 and the banner sat under the clock.

Validation:
- 15 host suites pass (ASan/UBSan), including new check-wow-sweep. Its Part A covers source invariants (emitted syscall tail, block-end flags, bridge bytes, stub order, park/unpark placement, registration and unregistration order, sweeper flag). Its Part B runs the production IosWowPark/IosWowUnpark/IosWowSyscallC against a model sweeper: a moved blocked call resumes at the dispatcher, an unmoved one returns, nested callbacks stay pinned, a stale stack is declined, a long-jumped depth is restored, and the rollback never parks.
- The FEX WOW64 build succeeded. The first build failed on a missing `.seh_nop` for the stub's first prologue instruction, which was fixed.
- The IPA printed "IPA verified". .xtool/verify-ml1430.py passes 26 checks: xtajit tags, the CodeResources seal of the new xtajit.dll, the Info.plist label, generated Library.swift in sync, same entry list as ml1420, and only Info.plist, the executable, xtajit.dll and the seal changed.
- No Wine, Steam or Windows program ran on this PC. Device-unverified. On device, look for `[gen-sweep] ... migrated=` with WoW64 threads and `[wow-sweep] ml1430 resumed`; the pool tail should stay near two live generations per process.

### 2026-09-23 - ml1440: JIT pool placement falls back to smaller sizes

Device result for ml1430 (logs 178, prev17, screenshot). The Library now shows the build label (`ml1430 · 09-23 02:09`). Neither launch could start Wine ("The session could not start").

Proven from the logs:
- The early pool (896 MB, "last session") and the session's own attempt both failed placement.
- Phase 1: the debugger's ANYWHERE pick was 0x7000000000 / 0x7038000000, inside the guest 64 GB window. It was rejected and blocked.
- Phase 2: none of the 160 FIXED probes in [0x119000000, 0x7000000000) was allocatable for 896 MB.
- The va-map's usable holes above the mode-A floor were 697, 608 and 292 MB (log 178) and 677 and 605 MB (prev17). In log 177 the same request had fit at 0x119400000.
- The map's "517934 MB hole" above 0x18d130000 is not evidence of free space: the region walk was truncated at 200001 entries, and [64 GB, 448 GB) is the GPU carve-out.
- Inferred: why every probe between 0x200000000 and 64 GB was refused is unknown, because the probe loop did not log refusals.
- ml1420's 896 MB floor for libraries with Windows client entries made this failure likelier. Before it, the startup size usually followed a 512 MB direct launch.

Fix (StikJITHelper.swift):
- allocatePool tries the requested size, then 768, 640 and 512 MB, but only while the debugger is attached and no pool is cached.
- The placement body is unchanged, now allocatePoolSized. Each fallback runs both phases again (about 2.4 s of debugger round trip per size in the worst case).
- `[jit-pool] ml1440 no home for N MB; trying M MB` / `fell back to M MB`. MADEIRA_POOL_FALLBACK=0 restores failing at the requested size.
- The Phase 2 "no home" line now carries the size and the first six vm_allocate refusals (address:kr, sampling above 0x200000000), so the next log can tell "occupied" from "not allocatable".
- Why a smaller pool is acceptable now: ml1430 lets the sweeper free pinned WoW64 generations, so the Steam client's steady-state tail should be a few generations per process rather than 720 MB. That is device-unverified.
- Workaround for ml1420/ml1430: Documents/madeira-pool.txt with `640` (the override skips the floor).

Validation:

- The IPA printed "IPA verified". .xtool/verify-ml1440.py passes 20 checks: generated StikJITHelper.swift in sync with the fallback, binary tags, the Info.plist label, the ml1430 xtajit.dll carried unchanged, and only the executable and Info.plist (and its seal) changed.

### 2026-09-23 - ml1450: how remote TCP connections end ([tcp-end]), saved errno on socket error paths

Device result for ml1440 (log 179, taken live while the session ran). Proven:
- **ml1430 works on device.** The early pool placed at 896 MB. `[wow-sweep] ml1430 syscall parking on` appears in every 32-bit process, and parked threads were resumed at the dispatcher after moves. `[gen-sweep]` ran to gen 54, moving 45-49 of 54 threads per sweep. The tail kept 4-5 of 12 carves free, with no TAIL REFUSED, no out-of-pool fault and no freeze; the user reported the app stayed responsive.
- Some threads are declined as "not parked: dispatcher sp X caller sp Y" with RSL about 0xdf0 below the caller. They stay pinned, as designed (inferred: a stale value left by a nested entry).

The Steam download bar stuck at 238 MB because the download stalled. Proven from the mirrored Steam logs:
- The client logged on at 02:29:58 and started depot 420 (3065 chunks) at 02:30:00, raising connections at rate 13.5 → 29.1.
- The CM WebSocket (27018) then dropped with `ConnectionDisconnected('I/O Operation Failed')` 8 s after logon. In the same second the client's own HTTP test of test.steampowered.com/204 failed ("HTTP fetch failed"). It reconnected at 02:30:10, logged on and dropped again at once.
- At 02:30:50: `BYieldingGetServersForSteamPipe failed (Transport Response Not Received / Result No Connection)` and `Failed to get list of download sources`.
- The CM socket (fd 1391) carried normal traffic through its last [sock-tl] snapshot and was then closed; fd 1391 was reused for a new port-443 connection 50 lines later. No socket error or peer close was recorded anywhere, so the cause is unknown.
- The connection-log mirror had spent all 96 lines within 15 s of the first logon.
- There were no EMFILE markers, and the highest fd seen was 1989 (so fd exhaustion is not supported, not excluded).

Changes:
- **`[tcp-end] ml1450`.** Stream sockets with a non-loopback peer; 48 lines per app lifetime each side; MADEIRA_TCP_END_TRACE=0.
  - ntdll socket.c ios_tcp_end_trace logs a zero-byte receive (peer closed) and any receive/send error other than would-block/EINTR, with local port, peer port and errno. Loopback is decided from the LOCAL address, because getpeername fails after a reset, which the host test showed: the first version silently skipped exactly the reset case. The peer port is printed as 0 when the peer is gone.
  - wineserver sock.c ios_tcp_close_trace in sock_destroy logs a connected remote socket's last close, with age and hangup/rd_shut/wr_shut/reset/aborted. This tells a program-initiated close of a healthy connection apart from one that had already failed.
- **Saved errno.** In try_recv/try_send the error path handed each probe (ios_sock_big_note, ios_sock_wire, ios_sock_tl, ios_loopback_io) a freshly read errno and then returned sock_errno_to_status(errno). The probes call getpeername/getsockname, which set errno when they fail, as on a reset connection, so the status the program saw could become "not connected" instead of "connection reset". The call's own error is now saved once and passed everywhere, including the returned status.
- **Steam log mirror.** IOS_STEAM_MIRROR_LINES = 320 for connection_log.txt and content_log.txt (was 96 each); both stay keyword-filtered.

Validation:
- The host suites pass (ASan/UBSan), including new check-tcp-end. Part A covers source invariants for the saved errno and the server close hook. Part B runs the production tracer on real sockets through a non-loopback interface address: peer close and reset (ECONNRESET, peer port 0) are logged; data, would-block, zero-length sends, loopback and datagram sockets are not; the 48-line cap holds; the rollback is silent.
- Native ntdll 35/35, win32u 46/46, server sock compiled. The IPA printed "IPA verified". .xtool/verify-ml1450.py passes 25 checks: workspace sync, archive and binary tags, the Info.plist label, same entry list as ml1440, only the executable and Info.plist (and seal) changed.
- No Wine, Steam or Windows program ran on this PC. The new lines are device-unverified.

### 2026-09-23 - ml1480: async I/O APCs for busy threads are handed over instead of dropped ([apc-requeue])

Device result for ml1470 (log 184). Proven:
- `[ordered-profile] ml1470` applied Multiblock=0, VectorTSOEnabled=1, HalfBarrierTSOEnabled=1 to steam.exe (reason=listed) and steamwebhelper.exe (reason=chromium-host), and `[fex-cfg]` agrees. "Unexpected error during startup" still appeared, so ordering was not the cause.
- `[accept-chain]` caught the failure on the 4th loopback accept:
  - the accept for thread 0094 completed while that thread was not in a server wait;
  - its APC_ASYNC_IO was not queued (`queued=0`);
  - the result was posted to the completion port with status 0x101 (STATUS_ALERTED), and thread 0090 dequeued it;
  - steam.exe never issued a receive on that connection. The helper sent its 554-byte request and waited.
  The three accepts whose thread was in a server wait were fine.

Root cause (proven from source, and consistent with the log):
- queue_apc sends SIGUSR1 to a thread that is not in an interruptible wait when its system APC queue is empty. On iOS, send_thread_signal always fails: get_process_port() is process->trace_data, which is always 0 here (see mach_ios.c).
- So queue_apc returned 0 and thread_apc_destroy completed the async with the call status. For an accept or receive, that status is STATUS_ALERTED with 0 bytes. The client half never ran: no accept addresses fetched, no recv done.
- A 0-byte successful TCP receive is EOF to the program. This probably also explains the WebSocket CM drops ("closed by program", no socket error, ~7 s after logon), while UDP CM sessions survive empty datagrams. That link is a hypothesis.

Change (wine/server/thread.c, WINE_IOS only):
- When the signal fails for an APC_ASYNC_IO, queue_apc now picks another thread of the same process that is in an interruptible, non-suspended server wait. If there is none, the APC stays on the issuing thread, which runs it at its next server wait.
- Why this is safe: the client half is process-scoped (get_async_result searches the process's asyncs; upstream already reroutes when the issuer has exited). async_wake_up alerts one async per queue at a time, so per-socket ordering holds.
- Other system APC types and process-wide APCs keep the upstream behaviour.
- `[apc-requeue] ml1480` logs the switch state and handovers (first 32, then every 1024th) with the APC status. MADEIRA_APC_REQUEUE=0 restores the drop.

Validation:
- New check-apc-requeue compiles the production queue_apc, is_in_apc_wait, get_apc_queue, is_thread_suspended and the ml1480 helpers, with a send_thread_signal that always fails. ASan/UBSan/LSan cover:
  - a busy issuer's APC goes to the waiting thread, which is woken;
  - with no waiter it stays on the issuer;
  - suspended, terminated and non-interruptible waiters are skipped;
  - a waiting issuer, or one with a non-empty queue, keeps the upstream path with no signal;
  - non-I/O system APCs and user APCs are unchanged;
  - the rollback reproduces the drop.
- All 19 host suites pass.
- Native ntdll 35/35, win32u 46/46, server thread compiled. The IPA printed "IPA verified".
- .xtool/verify-ml1480.py passes 25 checks against the ml1470 IPA:
  - workspace sync, and the server archive and binary tags;
  - no DRM-replacement names;
  - Info.plist label `ml1480 · 09-23 03:31`;
  - xtajit.dll unchanged;
  - same 1365 entries, with only the executable, Info.plist and the seal changed.
- No Wine, Steam or Windows program ran on this PC. ml1480 is device-unverified.

Changes:
- **DXMT (research/dxmt), `[d9-upload-commit] ml1490`.**
  - Texture uploads stage into m_uploadRing, whose blocks recycle only after the reading command buffer retires, and a load without Present never commits.
  - stageTextureUpload now counts staged bytes (reset on every commit). settleUploadPressure() commits once DXMT_D9_UPLOAD_COMMIT_MB (default 64; 0 disables) is reached. Before committing it waits for the previous upload commit's tail signal, so at most two thresholds are in flight. It then folds the completion event into m_cachedSignaled and trims the ring.
  - It is called only at boundaries where nothing is half recorded: the end of MTLD3D9Surface::UnlockRect, the start of UpdateTexture and UpdateSurface, and after a draw is queued (the existing rename-commit boundary). It is never called inside stageTextureUpload or the pre-draw managed sweep.
- **DXMT resource initializer, `[zero-buffer] ml1490`.**
  - The zero buffer grows to the next power of two (minimum 1 MB) instead of the exact request. Each growth costs a flushInternal().
  - The census now subtracts the replaced buffer.

Device result for ml1510 (logs 196 quiet, 197 extended logging; one game, client launch). Proven:

  - The client's web helper is still busy: Chrome_InProcRendererThread is about 16% of all CPU (94% JIT), plus CrBrowserMain, the GPU thread and COM STA threads.
  - The wineserver thread's request reads are about 19%, largely answering them.
  - The client's CGamepadAPITask is up to 10%.
- **Network polling continued through the game.** `[nsi-rate]` showed about 1,212 table reads and about 15,400 per-row gets per 10 s the whole session, i.e. about 40 GetAdaptersAddresses-shaped rounds a second (ndis/0, ipv4/10, ipv4/16).
  - With ml1510's device memo, NsiRequestChangeNotification (NotifyAddrChange) fails instantly with no device, which fits a wait-for-change-then-reread loop that never waits.
  - Which program runs the loop is not proven; `[nsi-rate]` now names it.
  - The client also logged network devices going away and coming back with changing ids (OnNetworkDeviceStateChange), consistent with polling.
- **The redistributable installers never ran.** SteamService /installscript (32-bit) took the third and last 4 GB guest window, so DXSETUP, PhysX_SystemSoftware and vcredist all failed at 'guest-window-reserve' (0xc0000017) within 40 ms. The client never records them as run, so it retries on every launch.
  - The failure itself is quick. The game's process was created 13.5 s after it, and nothing in the logs says what the client did in between (hence the console_log mirror below).
- **Browser logging.** The helper always ran with `--v=1 --log-severity=verbose`, formatting and writing every VLOG line in the quiet build as well.

Changes:
- **Helper park (ntdll signal_arm64_ios.c, process_ios.c, sync.c; app Library.swift).**
  - For a client-routed launch the app sets MADEIRA_PARK_EXES=steamwebhelper.exe and MADEIRA_PARK_OWNER_EXES=<client exe>.
  - When the app reports the game window (madeira_set_background_qos(1)) the park is armed. After MADEIRA_PARK_DELAY_S (default 10), the first listed thread to reach NtWait*/NtDelayExecution ends its process the way ExitProcess does, without DLL detach (NtTerminateProcess(0) then (-1); the FEX WOW64 BTCpuProcessTerm hook is empty). One thread per process does this.
  - The spawn gate refuses a listed image while armed (`[park] refused restart #n`).
  - A thread of the owner program calls ios_wow_reclaim_settled (virtual_ios.c) at most every 2 s until the dead window has been torn down. This is the release-on-next-adopt teardown run on demand, and only once every dead window has settled, so it never sleeps. Without it the memory would stay until the next 32-bit program starts, which during a game is never.
  - Kill switches: MADEIRA_STEAM_WEBHELPER_STOP=0 (app), MADEIRA_PARK=0 (ntdll).
  - Hypothesis to check on device: the client tolerates the helper's absence while a game runs (a Windows tool does the same) and the game keeps its Steam connection.
- **`[proc-mem] ml1520` (virtual_ios.c).** Every 30 s, for each 32-bit window, dirty and compressed pages via mach_vm_region_recurse, with the image name read by mach_vm_read_overwrite. Also the footprint outside all windows. MADEIRA_PROC_MEM=0 disables it.
- **nsi.dll: change requests stay pending (i386/aarch64/arm64ec).**
  - With no device and the fallback present, an overlapped request is left STATUS_PENDING with its event reset, and the returned handle is a private never-signalled event. A synchronous request waits.
  - NsiCancelChangeNotification completes a pending one with STATUS_CANCELLED and sets its event.
  - MADEIRA_NSI_NOTIFY_PENDING=0 fails requests as before.
  - `[nsi-rate]` gains `by (ml1520) image/tid=n`, the top reading threads.
- **Browser logging.** Verbose only when diagnostics are on (madeira_diag_on) or MADEIRA_CEF_QUIET_LOG=0; otherwise `--log-severity=warning`. `[cef-logging]` reports `verbose=`.
- **`[steam-console] ml1520` (ntdll file.c).** Mirrors the client's console_log.txt lines naming launch tasks (GameAction ... changed task to ..., Game process ...), with the usual 320-line budget and account masking.
- **Starting screen.** New stages from console_log.txt tasks: needs input (license agreement / CD key / dialog), installers (install script), cloud sync (Synchronizing cloud), and game starting (CreatingProcess / WaitingGameWindow / Completed).
- **UI (owner requests).**

  - Game details: the Steam section sits under library details, and the picker says "Steam client" with a footer naming the Windows client.

### 2026-09-23 - ml1570: correction — the tablet's single guest window was the band, not the entitlement

- **ml1560 conclusion withdrawn.** It blamed the missing extended-virtual-addressing entitlement. The owner's phone logs `extended-virtual-addressing: false` too (log 204) and runs Steam fine; its map simply reaches 0x8000000000 (512 GB). The tablet's map ends at 0xfc0000000 (63 GB).
- **What limits the tablet (proven from its log):**
  - The small-map band was hard-limited to two candidates, [0x400000000, 0x600000000).
  - iOS refused the second (0x500000000), although mach_vm_region showed it free and the startup probe had mapped it. After graphics and pool setup even 16 KB at 0x100010000 failed with ENOMEM, so some ranges are claimed invisibly after startup.
  - One window was left, and the installer's 32-bit helper could not start.
- **Change (virtual_ios.c):**
  - On a small map the band is [16 GB, 44 GB), below the FEX host arena at 48 GB and its guard.
  - Session start takes up to MADEIRA_WOW_SMALL_VA_SLOTS placeholders (default 4), skipping any slot iOS refuses. =2 restores the old two-slot band.
  - Placeholders are PROT_NONE reservations; a 16 GB budget in a 63 GB map leaves the top-down furniture its room.
- **Setup's extended-VA warning (ml1560) removed.**
- **Validation:** new check-small-va-band compiles the production ios_wow_band for 63 GB and 512 GB maps and checks the switch and the placeholder cap. 30 suites pass.
- .xtool/verify-ml1570.py passes 24 checks against the ml1560 IPA: label `ml1570 · 09-23 19:38`, native 35/35 + 46/46, only the executable, Info.plist and the seal changed. Device-unverified.

### 2026-09-23 - ml1590: is_wow64() followed a session global; running 32-bit programs lost their CPU area

Device results for ml1580. Proven:
- **Phone log 206.** The new client's first thread got `[wow-init-ctx] status 0xc000000d Esp 0` on all 64 retries, then exit c000000d.
- **Tablet log 6.** Four windows were reserved (0x4, 0x6, 0x8, 0xa). The installer then faulted in wow64.dll+0x1b3f8 (a user-callback path) writing guest 0xffffffb0, a 32-bit stack of 0, after a 64-bit child (winemenubuilder) started and exited; the installer stalled at 25-30%. Phone log 202's `0x71ffffffb0` faults are the same shape.
- **The mechanism.**
  - ThreadWow64Context → get_thread_wow64_context → get_cpu_area() returns NULL when is_wow64() is false.
  - On iOS, is_wow64() is `!!wow_peb`, a SESSION global that `[wow-peb]` clears when a 32-bit window is released and restores or swaps around 64-bit child starts.
  - A 32-bit program still running then lost its own CPU-area context.

Change: under WINE_IOS, is_wow64() is TRUE for a thread whose own TEB has WowTebOffset set, before falling back to the global. Switch: ios_wow64_by_teb, MADEIRA_WOW64_BY_TEB=0; `[wow64-by-teb] ml1590 on|off` is logged at virtual_init.

Validation: 30 suites pass; native 35/35 + 46/46; the IPA printed "IPA verified". .xtool/verify-ml1590.py passes against the ml1580 IPA (label `ml1590 · 09-23 20:01`). Device-unverified.
